conversation.content: Read historical page 59 and compare its cloud definition with Wikipedia. Cite exact bri-/wiki- source IDs. Keep the answer to three sentences.

Historical page 59 (Britannica Sixth edition, Volume 6) defines a cloud as "a collection of vapours suspended in the atmosphere" and discusses cloud formation in terms of latent heat, condensation, and an unsettled theory attributing it to electricity [bri-0059-891965a7ca3e]. The Wikipedia disambiguation page defines a cloud as "a visible mass of condensed droplets or frozen crystals suspended in the atmosphere," offering a straightforward descriptive definition without addressing electrical causation [wiki-593754-1320064819-5941026ced18]. The two agree that clouds are suspended atmospheric masses, but the historical entry treats clouds as a causal meteorological problem while the Wikipedia corpus provides only a brief disambiguation definition rather than a full modern meteorological article.
Which causal direction did that historical author leave unresolved? One sentence, cite the source.

The author left unresolved whether clouds are formed because vapours are first electrically compounded, or whether they become electrified only after being separated from and condensed out of the atmosphere [bri-0059-891965a7ca3e].
Which historical page were we discussing, and what uncertainty did you identify? Use the existing conversation; answer in one sentence.

We were discussing Britannica historical page 59 (bri-0059-891965a7ca3e), and the uncertainty was whether clouds are formed because vapours are first electrically compounded or whether they become electrified only after being separated from and condensed out of the atmosphere.
